evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Periodic KYC reviews that hold up when the examiner asks.' plus a lede saying it finds who is due, gathers what is on file, and asks members only for what is missing. 'Built for credit unions with 20,000 to 200,000 members' sits under the CTAs. The what and the who are clear by the end of the lede. The headline alone does not say who it is for.
evidence.fit: Every explicit ask is met. 'Book a demo' goes to https://refresh.example/demo in the header, hero and closing. A dark band titled 'The risk decision stays with your compliance officer' covers the officer-decides line. 'Questions your examiner will ask' gives six Q&A pairs. 'Where Refresh is today' says the two pilots are unnamed and there are no measured results. Steps carry 'Done by Refresh / checked by member-service staff', and 'What the member sees' covers members. The tone is calm and right for compliance.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero review file is its own idea: a ledger with a red margin rule, pencil ticks drawn down the margin on load, a legend of marks and an italic officer signature. Below the hero the structure is the familiar kit: a Today/With Refresh comparison table, five numbered steps, a dark two-column band of checklists, a two-column Q&A grid, a status table and a CTA band. Remove the hero and it could be most B2B compliance pages.
evidence.proof: The sample review file is in the first screen at 1440 (x 731 to 1262, y 157 onward) and labelled 'Sample'. It shows selection, three on-file checks, one stale item, the request, the member reply and the officer decision, and its dates are consistent (last reviewed Nov 2025, 12-month cycle, due Nov 4 2026, next due Oct 2027). It is completely static: nothing responds, so a visitor cannot step through it. At 390 it starts below the first viewport.
evidence.craft: Clean and consistent: tokenised colours, ruled sections, a coherent green and ink palette, and the pencil-mark motif reused in the band and legend. Type is a system stack (Avenir Next / Segoe UI / Inter, with a Charter/Cambria serif body) and no fonts are shipped, so the look changes by OS. At 1440 the left hero column leaves about 200px of empty space under the CTAs next to the tall file. The 'Member replied online' mark (a tick with a stray dash) reads as a glitch. The header 'Book a demo' is 37px tall.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow and type stays readable (smallest 12px). The comparison table recomposes into Today/With Refresh labelled blocks, and the file drops its margin rule and goes to two columns. However, the nav links are display:none under 760px and no menu replaces them, so 'How a review runs', 'For your examiner' and 'Where we are' cannot be reached from the header. The sample file starts around y 650, below the first screen. The header CTA is 37px tall and 'See how a review runs' is 26px. The page is 8,698px of mostly single-column text.
evidence.honesty: A 'Sample' chip is on the file at every width, and the footer reads 'The member, staff and credit union details on this page are samples.' The status table states 'Measured results: None yet' and 'Two credit unions, unnamed at their request'. Disclosure works partly through a section listing what the company lacks. The member-request mock ('This takes about two minutes', 'Lakeview Logistics') has no sample label of its own.
evidence.interaction: The only controls are links. I clicked the hero 'Book a demo' (it requested https://refresh.example/demo) and 'See how a review runs' (it scrolled #how to the top). There is nothing to operate in the product artifact: the file is a static figure with a one-time load animation. The member request has a styled 'Update my details' span that looks like a button but does nothing. At 390 and 768 there is no mobile menu, so section navigation is lost.
evidence.copy: Plain and specific: 'Expected monthly cash deposits / A rough range is fine', 'When an examiner asks who decided, the answer is a named person at your credit union', and examiner questions phrased the way an examiner would ask them. No buzzwords. The same four-part description (due / on file / ask / record) is repeated in the lede, comparison table, steps, band and Q&A, so the middle of the page reads as restatement.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, the demo CTA and the sample file showing a full review are all in view, which makes the promise believable. 390: the headline, lede and 'Book a demo' fit, but the artifact is not visible; only the page background is below the 'Built for...' line at 600px. The promise is strong at desktop but unproven at phone width.

problems: The product artifact is static and there is no other interactive element, so a visitor cannot step through a review. At 390 the artifact also falls below the first screen.
No mobile navigation: header section links are hidden under 760px with no menu, and tap targets are under 44px (header CTA 37px, secondary link 26px).
Below the hero the structure is generic (comparison table, numbered steps, dark checklist band, Q&A grid, CTA band), and the same description repeats from section to section.

evidence.clarity: 1440: the H1 'KYC reviews your examiner can follow' sits beside a bold 'Refresh is periodic KYC review software for credit unions.' followed by what it does and a 'Book a demo' button. The what, who and next step are all in the first two lines. Every later section restates one examiner question rather than introducing new framing.
evidence.fit: Each section opens with an 'Examiner:' question ('How do you decide who is due?', 'Who decided this risk rating?', 'Show me what happened, in order.'). That directly addresses the brief's 'reassure a compliance officer who will be asked by examiners'. The officer-decides constraint is in the hero note, in the artifact ('Refresh doesn't make this call') and in a duties table where 'Decide the member's risk rating' reads 'No' under Refresh. Staff appear in the due-list section, and members get a sample request. Pilot status and the lack of numbers are stated in the hero and the closing section.
evidence.distinctiveness: The page's motif comes from the product: a manila folder with five step tabs, a 'The same step today' pane showing the Reviews_2026.xlsx row ('OK per MC, see email'), a mono ledger font for dates and trail entries, D/F/S/R/O trail glyphs, and line drawings of the mailed update form with an 'LM x2' sticky note and an 'EXAM PREP' binder. With the logo removed it is still recognisably this product. The drawings are the most decorative element, but each carries the 'today' half of a before/after.
evidence.proof: An operable sample review fills the bottom half of the first screen at 1440 and the area below the CTA at 390, labelled 'Sample review · Fictional member. Pick a step.' I clicked steps 1 to 5 at each width. The status chips go from Not checked to On file/Missing to Asked to Received, the tally ('3 on file, 2 missing') and trail count (1, 2, 3, 5, 6 entries) update, and the officer box switches from 'waiting for a complete file' to the signed decision. The dates hold together across the page: last review 2024-10-14, 24-month Moderate schedule, due 2026-10-14, decided 2026-10-08, next review 2028-10-08, and the same member appears in the due list, sample request and trail.
evidence.craft: Embedded Lora, Inter and a mono face, used with a clear scale. The manila, ink and blue palette is restrained, and the yellow highlight marks what changed. Hierarchy is sharp at 1440 and 768. Small flaws: the artifact's mono detail text is 13px and dense; at 390 the highlighted J. Alvarez row in the due list paints as separate cell blocks with gaps rather than one band; desktop nav and footer links are 32px tall.
evidence.mobile: 390: the layout is recomposed rather than shrunk. The header has the Book a demo button and a Menu button (44px); the menu opened, Escape closed it, and tapping 'Exam trail' closed it and scrolled to the section. The tabs become a 5-up grid of 52px buttons, and the artifact is visible in the first viewport. Step feedback appears immediately below the tabs; the 'says' line sat at y 244 after the tap. The due list and duties table become cards, the binder drawing is dropped, and nothing overflows at 390 or 320. The spreadsheet 'today' pane sits below the long 'now' pane, so the comparison is less visible on phone.
evidence.honesty: Labels sit where the example appears: 'Fictional member', 'Sample October list... Fictional members', 'Example values. Yours are set by your compliance officer', 'Riverbend Credit Union (fictional)', 'Sample trail'. The hero states 'Refresh is in pilot at two credit unions.' The closing section explains why there are no numbers, and the CTA note says 'Opens the demo booking page at refresh.example.' before the click.
evidence.interaction: Tabs are real buttons with aria-pressed. Mouse clicks worked at all three widths; Enter on a focused tab and Tab plus Space both switched steps. A polite live region announces the step text, and items that changed flash yellow. The mobile menu handles Escape, outside click and focus leaving it. No console or page errors at any width. All five 'Book a demo' links resolve to https://refresh.example/demo. Minor: no arrow-key movement between tabs, and the mini-trail pane only exists at 1000px and up.
evidence.copy: Specific nouns from the customer's world: 'OK per MC, see email', 'called, left msg x2', 'Someone filters the sheet by next-due date and trusts that the column is current.', 'ID on file expired 2026-08-31', 'employer field is blank'. Buttons and labels say what they do ('Read the full trail', 'Pick a step'). The officer-decides line recurs several times, but deliberately.

problems: On phone the 'same step today' spreadsheet pane is pushed below the long Refresh pane, so the before/after inside the artifact is mostly lost at 390.
The artifact's mono detail text is 13px and dense, and at 390 the highlighted due-list row renders as fragmented cell blocks.
Desktop nav and footer links are 32px tall, and the tabs lack arrow-key navigation.

reason: B turns the brief's central tension (reassuring an officer who will face examiners) into the structure of the page: every section answers an examiner question, and a steppable sample review in the first screen at both widths shows what is checked, asked, received and decided, with consistent dates and fictional labels. A is honest and well-toned, but its artifact is static, it has no mobile navigation, and most of its structure is the standard template. I would change my mind only if B's step interaction failed on real touch devices, which I could not reproduce here.
